c: Scarborough’s rental towers hold tenants for decades, and a unit vacated after thirty years is a fundamentally different job from a standard turnover. The apartment blocks along Kingston Road, Markham Road and Lawrence East were built in the 1960s and 70s, and many residents have been in the same unit since. When one comes back, it contains a lifetime rather than a lease term — furniture in every room, decades of stored belongings, and a locker downstairs nobody has opened in years. We assess these units in person and quote for the real volume, because a floor plan tells you nothing about what is behind the closet doors.

The buildings themselves add the second constraint. One service elevator serves the entire tower, corridors are narrow, and refuse chutes will not take furniture or appliances. Everything leaves through the same route inside the same booked window. Away from the corridors, Scarborough has one of the highest concentrations of basement apartments in Toronto — owner-occupied houses across Agincourt, Malvern, West Hill, Woburn and Bendale where the landlord lives upstairs. Those need separate-entrance routing and respect for the household. We schedule every tenant turnover cleanout backwards from your listing date and photograph the condition before anything is removed.

blocks.text: Common Questions About Property Management Cleanout in Scarborough

c: Scarborough has a mix of rental towers, basement apartments, detached rental homes, townhouses, and multi-unit properties. Long-term tenants can also leave behind a substantial volume of belongings, making professional property management cleanouts useful between tenancies, before renovations, or ahead of a new listing.

items.q: Read What People Ask About Property Management Cleanout in Scarborough
a: 1. What does a property management cleanout in Scarborough involve?

A property management cleanout involves removing unwanted furniture, appliances, mattresses, boxes, electronics, household belongings, and other approved items from a rental property. We can clear an entire unit or specific areas such as lockers, basements, garages, and storage spaces.
2. When should a rental property be cleared after a tenant moves out?

The cleanout should be scheduled after the tenancy has ended and the property manager has confirmed which belongings are authorized for removal. Clearing the property early gives landlords more time for cleaning, repairs, inspections, and preparing for the next tenant.
3. How can landlords prepare a unit for the next occupant?

We can remove leftover furniture, appliances, boxes, clutter, and other unwanted belongings. Once the unit is cleared, it can be cleaned, inspected, repaired, photographed, and prepared for the incoming tenant.
4. Who removes belongings that tenants leave behind?

Landlords and property managers can hire a professional cleanout company to remove authorized tenant belongings. Before removal, the property manager should confirm that any abandoned items can legally be disposed of.
5. What happens to abandoned items after a tenant vacates?

The landlord or property manager should first follow the applicable requirements for handling abandoned tenant property. Once removal is authorized, we can sort and remove furniture, household items, appliances, boxes, and other unwanted contents.
6. Can property managers arrange a cleanout following an eviction?

Yes. We can assist with property cleanouts following an authorized eviction or other approved move-out situation. The property manager should confirm that the required legal process has been completed before removal begins.
7. Can a rental unit be cleared before the next tenant’s move-in date?

Yes. We can schedule the cleanout between tenants so the property is cleared before the new occupant arrives. The timing can be planned around cleaning, repairs, inspections, and the confirmed move-in date.
8. How can a vacant property be prepared for new tenant showings?

Removing unwanted furniture, boxes, clutter, and leftover belongings can make rooms easier to access and present. We can clear the property before showings so prospective tenants see the available space rather than the previous tenant’s possessions.
9. What types of properties can receive professional cleanout services?
We handle rental towers, condos, apartments, detached houses, basement apartments, townhouses, and other managed properties. Partial and full-property cleanouts can both be arranged.
10. Can detached rental homes be emptied after tenant turnover?

Yes. Detached rental homes can be cleared after an authorized tenant turnover. We can remove contents from bedrooms, living spaces, kitchens, basements, garages, and other areas included in the cleanout.
11. Are condos and apartment units included in property cleanouts?

Yes. Condo and apartment cleanouts are included, from individual units to larger multi-unit turnover projects. For high-rise buildings, we can plan the job around service elevators, loading areas, building access, and required paperwork.
12. Can townhouses be cleared before they are rented again?
Yes. Townhouses can be emptied between tenants, including bedrooms, living areas, kitchens, basements, garages, and storage spaces. We can work within the available turnover window.
13. What furniture can be removed from a managed property?

We can remove many common household furnishings, including sofas, chairs, tables, beds, dressers, cabinets, wardrobes, shelving, and other unwanted furniture. Larger pieces can be dismantled when necessary.
14. Can couches, tables, chairs, and cabinets be hauled away?

Yes. These common household items can be included in the cleanout. Our crew handles the lifting, carrying, loading, and hauling instead of requiring the property manager to arrange separate furniture pickups.
15. Who removes mattresses and unwanted bedroom furniture?

Our crew can remove mattresses, bed frames, dressers, nightstands, wardrobes, and other unwanted bedroom items. Multiple bedrooms can be cleared during the same visit when included in the agreed scope.
16. Can tenant-left appliances be taken out of a rental unit?
Yes, eligible appliances can be removed. Depending on the item, this can include refrigerators, freezers, washers, dryers, stoves, ovens, and other household appliances.
17. Can boxes and miscellaneous household belongings be removed?

Yes. We can clear boxes, household goods, personal belongings, general clutter, and other unwanted contents left behind after a tenancy. This is especially helpful after a long-term tenancy where belongings have accumulated over many years.
18. Can closets and storage areas be emptied during the cleanout?
Yes. Closets, storage rooms, lockers, and other storage areas can be included. We recommend identifying these spaces when the job is booked so the full volume can be assessed.
19. Can basement contents be cleared along with the rest of the property?

Yes. Basement furniture, boxes, appliances, household items, and other approved belongings can be removed during the same cleanout. Basement apartments can also be handled separately from the owner’s living space when required.
20. Can garage and outdoor storage contents be removed?
Yes. Garages, sheds, exterior storage spaces, and other areas can be included when they are part of the agreed scope. We can plan the removal around driveway and property access.
21. Are unwanted patio, balcony, or yard items included?
Yes, eligible outdoor belongings can be included in the cleanout. Patio furniture, outdoor household items, seasonal belongings, and certain yard waste can be handled depending on the material.
22. Can a property be emptied before repairs or renovations begin?

Yes. Removing unwanted contents before contractors arrive gives them more room to work. We can clear furniture, appliances, household belongings, and other approved materials before maintenance or renovation work begins.
23. Who clears unwanted contents before contractors arrive?

The landlord or property manager can arrange a professional cleanout before the contractor’s scheduled start date. Our crew handles the lifting and hauling so contractors can begin with clearer access to the work areas.
24. Can a cleanout be scheduled before an inspection or property showing?

Yes. A cleanout can be completed before an inspection, appraisal, or showing when unwanted contents are affecting access or presentation. We can concentrate on the rooms and storage areas that need to be cleared.
25. How can landlords prepare a rental for listing photographs?

Removing excess furniture, boxes, clutter, and leftover tenant belongings can make the property look more open and easier to photograph. We can complete the cleanout before the photographer arrives and leave the unit swept and empty.
26. Can a property manager arrange a cleanout between short lease periods?

Yes. Short turnover periods can be accommodated when the property size, volume, and access allow. For Scarborough rental towers, elevator availability should be confirmed early because the booked service-elevator window can affect the removal schedule.
27. What can managers do when a rental needs to be cleared urgently?
Contact us with the property location, approximate volume, access details, and required completion date. Same-day service may be available when scheduling and access permit.
28. Can multiple rental units be scheduled for cleanout service?

Yes. Multiple units can be scheduled together, including several apartments in the same building. We can coordinate the work around one elevator booking and consolidate the cleanout schedule where building access allows.
29. Is recurring cleanout service available for property management companies?

Yes. Property managers with frequent tenant turnovers can arrange ongoing cleanout support. Recurring service can help with furniture removal, abandoned belongings, move-out cleanouts, and preparation between tenants.
30. Can landlords schedule service without being physically present?

Yes. A landlord or property manager does not necessarily need to stay at the property during the cleanout. Access instructions and the approved removal scope can be arranged in advance, and photo documentation can be provided after the work.
31. How can access be arranged for the cleanout crew?

Access can be provided through a property manager, tenant, superintendent, concierge, lockbox, key, or another authorized representative. For apartment buildings, service-elevator and loading-area arrangements should be confirmed before the appointment.
32. Can cleanout appointments work around condo building access restrictions?

Yes. We can coordinate cleanouts around service-elevator reservations, loading areas, building rules, and other access restrictions. Where required, insurance documentation can also be provided before the scheduled work.
33. How long does it usually take to empty a rental property?

The timeframe depends on the property size, amount of material, number of rooms, and access conditions. A small apartment can be relatively straightforward, while a long-term tenant turnover in a rental tower may involve considerably more furniture and belongings.
34. Does the property manager need to sort the contents beforehand?
Not necessarily. We can handle the sorting as part of the cleanout. However, the property manager should identify anything that must remain at the property before our crew begins.
35. Who handles heavy lifting and bulky furniture?

Our crew handles the heavy lifting, carrying, loading, and hauling. We can move bulky furniture and appliances through stairs, hallways, entrances, elevators, and other access routes required for the job.
36. Can large items be removed from high-rise or upper-floor units?

Yes. Large furniture, mattresses, appliances, and other approved bulky items can be removed from upper-floor units. In Scarborough rental towers, we plan the crew and removal route around the available service-elevator window.
37. What happens to usable belongings found during the cleanout?

Usable items are checked for donation opportunities before recycling or disposal. Items in serviceable condition may be directed to donation partners so they can potentially be reused instead of immediately becoming waste.
38. Can recyclable materials be separated from unwanted rental contents?
Yes. Where practical, eligible metal, electronics, and other recyclable materials can be separated from general waste. The handling method depends on the material and its condition.
39. Can property managers receive photos after the cleanout is finished?

Yes. Photo documentation is included with Scarborough property management cleanouts. Property managers can use the timestamped photos and written removal record for their property files, turnover records, or documentation of the unit’s condition.
40. How can I request a property management cleanout quote in Scarborough?
You can contact Live Junk Free at

or request a quote online. Provide the Scarborough property location, property type, approximate volume, areas to be cleared, access requirements, and preferred completion date so we can assess the job and confirm the cleanout scope.
